resource.name: aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application
resource.description: Manages a Kinesis Analytics v2 Application. This resource can be used to manage both Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL applications and Kinesis Data Analytics for Apache Flink applications. Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL applications created using this resource cannot currently be viewed in the AWS Console. To manage Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL applications that can also be viewed in the AWS Console, use the aws_kinesis_analytics_application resource.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` Terraform resource enables the creation and management of Kinesis Data Analytics v2 applications, supporting both SQL-based and Apache Flink-based stream processing workloads. It is commonly used for building real-time data analytics pipelines, processing and transforming streaming data, and integrating with Kinesis Data Streams or other data sources. Users can configure application runtime environments, input/output data sources, logging, checkpointing, and scaling settings to optimize performance and reliability for complex stream processing use cases.

examples.title: Apache Flink Application
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an Apache Flink application using the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource in Terraform, including integration with an S3 bucket for application code storage, custom environment properties, and advanced Flink-specific configurations such as checkpointing, monitoring, and parallelism settings. It illustrates the use of `application_code_configuration`, `environment_properties`, and `flink_application_configuration` blocks to set up a scalable, debug-enabled Flink runtime environment with auto-scaling and custom metrics.

examples.title: SQL Application
examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS Kinesis Data Analytics SQL application (`aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application`) with multiple inputs, outputs, and reference data sources. It showcases key configurations such as SQL application code, input schema with CSV mapping, output destinations to Lambda and Firehose, and integration with S3 for reference data, along with CloudWatch logging for monitoring.

examples.title: VPC Configuration
examples.llm_summary: "Demonstrates how to configure an AWS Kinesis Data Analytics v2 application to run a Flink application within a VPC, using the `vpc_configuration` block to specify security group IDs and subnet IDs. Includes integration with an S3 bucket for application code storage and retrieval via the `application_code_configuration` block, showcasing the use of `s3_content_location` for code deployment."

arguments.name: application_mode
arguments.description: (Optional) The application's mode. Valid values are `STREAMING`, `INTERACTIVE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `application_mode` argument for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to specify the operational mode of the application, either `STREAMING` for real-time data processing or `INTERACTIVE` for on-demand querying and analysis. Configuring this argument determines the application's behavior and use case, enabling users to tailor the application to either continuous data streams or interactive workloads based on their analytics requirements.

arguments.name: description
arguments.description: (Optional) A summary description of the application.
arguments.llm_summary: The `description` argument for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to define a human-readable summary that provides context or metadata about the application. Setting this argument helps document the application's purpose or functionality, aiding in resource organization and identification within the AWS environment.

arguments.name: force_stop
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to force stop an unresponsive Flink-based application.
arguments.llm_summary: The `force_stop` argument for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to control whether a Flink-based application should be forcibly terminated if it becomes unresponsive. Setting this argument to `true` ensures immediate shutdown of the application, which can be useful for managing stuck processes or recovering from critical failures, aligning with lifecycle management and operational recovery goals.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to specify a unique identifier for the application, enabling precise referencing and management within Terraform configurations. While optional, setting this argument can help users track and distinguish the application resource in complex deployments or when integrating with other infrastructure components.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: (Required) The name of the in-application stream.
arguments.llm_summary: The `name` argument specifies the unique identifier for the in-application stream within the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource. By defining this required string, users establish the stream's name, which serves as a reference point for configuring data processing workflows, enabling interaction with other application components, and ensuring proper resource identification within the Kinesis Analytics V2 application.

arguments.name: runtime_environment
arguments.description: (Required) The runtime environment for the application. Valid values: `SQL-1_0`, `FLINK-1_6`, `FLINK-1_8`, `FLINK-1_11`, `FLINK-1_13`, `FLINK-1_15`, `FLINK-1_18`, `FLINK-1_19`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `runtime_environment` argument specifies the execution framework for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application`, allowing users to define the underlying processing engine (e.g., SQL or Apache Flink versions) that powers the application's data analytics capabilities. Setting this argument determines the application's compatibility with specific runtime features and processing behaviors, enabling users to tailor the environment to their data streaming and analytics requirements.

arguments.name: service_execution_role
arguments.description: (Required) The ARN of the IAM role used by the application to access Kinesis data streams, Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams, Amazon S3 objects, and other external resources.
arguments.llm_summary: The `service_execution_role` argument specifies the ARN of the IAM role that grants the Kinesis Data Analytics application permissions to access external resources such as Kinesis data streams, Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams, and Amazon S3 objects. Setting this required argument ensures the application can securely interact with these services, enabling data processing and integration workflows.

arguments.name: start_application
arguments.description: (Optional) Whether to start or stop the application.
arguments.llm_summary: The `start_application` argument for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to control the application's runtime state by specifying whether the application should be started or stopped upon creation or update. Setting this argument to `true` ensures the application begins processing data streams immediately, aligning with user goals of automating application lifecycle management and operational readiness.

arguments.name: tags
arguments.description: (Optional) A map of tags to assign to the application. If configured with a provider `default_tags` configuration block present, tags with matching keys will overwrite those defined at the provider-level. The application_configuration object supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags` argument for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to assign key-value metadata to the application, enabling organization, categorization, and resource tracking for purposes such as cost allocation, environment identification, or compliance. When configured, these tags can override provider-level default tags, offering granular control over resource labeling.

arguments.name: tags_all
arguments.llm_summary: The `tags_all` argument for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to define a comprehensive set of key-value tags that are automatically merged with resource-specific tags, enabling consistent metadata management across AWS resources. By configuring this argument, users can streamline tagging for purposes like cost allocation, resource organization, and access control policies, ensuring alignment with broader tagging strategies.

blocks.name: application_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) The application's configuration

blocks.name: application_code_configuration
blocks.description: (Required) The code location and type parameters for the application.

arguments.name: code_content_type
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies whether the code content is in text or zip format. Valid values: `PLAINTEXT`, `ZIPFILE`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `code_content_type` argument in the `application_code_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource specifies the format of the application code, allowing users to define whether the code is provided as plaintext (`PLAINTEXT`) or a compressed archive (`ZIPFILE`). This configuration ensures the application can correctly interpret and process the code during deployment, aligning with user goals of managing code delivery formats for streaming data applications.

blocks.name: code_content
blocks.description: (Optional) The location and type of the application code.  The code_content object supports the following:

arguments.description: (Optional) The text-format code for the application. The s3_content_location object supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `text_content` argument allows users to define the application code directly in plain text format for an AWS Kinesis Data Analytics v2 application. This provides an alternative to specifying code via an S3 location, enabling users to embed and configure the application's logic or processing scripts inline within the Terraform configuration.

blocks.name: s3_content_location

By defining this required parameter, users enable the application to access and retrieve content from the designated S3 bucket, ensuring proper initialization and execution of the Kinesis Data Analytics application.

arguments.name: file_key
arguments.description: (Required) The object key name containing the reference data. The vpc_configuration object supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `file_key` argument specifies the exact object key name within an S3 bucket that contains reference data for the Kinesis Analytics application. By defining this required parameter, users ensure the application can access and utilize the specified data source for processing or analytics, enabling functionality such as streaming data enrichment or real-time insights.

arguments.name: object_version
arguments.description: (Optional) The version of the object containing the application code. The application_snapshot_configuration object supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `object_version` argument allows users to specify a specific version of the S3 object containing the application code for the Kinesis Analytics V2 application. By defining this, users can control which version of the code is deployed, enabling precise version management and rollback capabilities for application updates or snapshots.

blocks.llm_summary: The `s3_content_location` block within the `code_content` configuration of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource specifies the Amazon S3 bucket and object details that store the application code. This block enables users to define the source location for application artifacts, facilitating seamless integration of code hosted in S3 for deployment and execution in Kinesis Data Analytics applications.

The `code_content` configuration block within `application_code_configuration` for the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource specifies the location and type of the application code, enabling users to define how and where the application retrieves its executable code. This block encapsulates settings related to code storage, such as inline code or external sources (e.g., S3), allowing users to manage the deployment and execution of streaming analytics applications with precise control over code accessibility and versioning.

The `application_code_configuration` block within the `application_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource defines the code source and type for the application, enabling users to specify where the application code resides (e.g., S3 or inline) and how it is executed. This configuration is essential for managing the application's runtime behavior and ensuring the correct code is deployed, supporting use cases like real-time data processing and analytics workflows.

Enabling this feature ensures the application can periodically save its state, supporting fault tolerance and recovery, which is critical for maintaining data processing continuity in event-driven architectures.

blocks.llm_summary: The `application_snapshot_configuration` block within the `application_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource enables the management of snapshot functionality for Flink-based applications, allowing users to persist application state for fault tolerance and recovery. By configuring this block, users can define whether snapshots are enabled, ensuring stateful processing continuity and minimizing data loss during application restarts or failures.

By specifying this map, users can control operational parameters such as resource allocation, application behavior, or custom configurations, enabling fine-grained management of the application's execution environment.

This block enables users to customize and control application behavior by specifying environment-specific settings, facilitating fine-grained adjustments to optimize application performance and functionality in Kinesis Data Analytics.

Configuring this block allows for tailored control over the application's execution context, optimizing performance and compatibility with specific workloads or integrations."

blocks.name: flink_application_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) The configuration of a Flink-based application.

blocks.name: checkpoint_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Describes an application's checkpointing configuration.

arguments.name: checkpoint_interval
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes the interval in milliseconds between checkpoint operations.
arguments.llm_summary: The `checkpoint_interval` argument in the `checkpoint_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to define the time interval, in milliseconds, between checkpoint operations for the application. Configuring this interval impacts the application's fault tolerance and recovery behavior by controlling how frequently state data is saved, which is critical for ensuring data consistency and minimizing loss during failures.

arguments.name: checkpointing_enabled
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes whether checkpointing is enabled for a Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics application.
arguments.llm_summary: "Controls whether checkpointing is activated for a Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics application, enabling state persistence and fault tolerance by periodically saving application state. Useful for configuring reliable data processing workflows and ensuring recovery in case of application failures."

arguments.name: configuration_type
arguments.description: (Required) Describes whether the application uses the default parallelism for the Kinesis Data Analytics service. Valid values: `CUSTOM`, `DEFAULT`. Set this attribute to `CUSTOM` in order for any specified `auto_scaling_enabled`, `parallelism`, or `parallelism_per_kpu` attribute values to be effective.
arguments.llm_summary: The `configuration_type` argument in the `checkpoint_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource specifies whether the application uses default parallelism settings (`DEFAULT`) or custom-defined parallelism (`CUSTOM`). Setting this argument to `CUSTOM` enables users to configure advanced scaling properties such as `auto_scaling_enabled`, `parallelism`, and `parallelism_per_kpu`, allowing fine-grained control over the application's performance and resource allocation.

arguments.name: min_pause_between_checkpoints
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes the minimum time in milliseconds after a checkpoint operation completes that a new checkpoint operation can start.
arguments.llm_summary: "min_pause_between_checkpoints" in the "checkpoint_configuration" of the "aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application" resource allows users to define the minimum time interval (in milliseconds) between the completion of one checkpoint operation and the start of the next. This argument helps control the frequency of checkpointing, optimizing application performance and resource utilization by preventing overly frequent checkpoint operations.

blocks.llm_summary: The `checkpoint_configuration` block within the `flink_application_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource defines settings for managing Flink application's checkpointing behavior, which ensures fault tolerance and state consistency during stream processing. By configuring this block, users can control checkpoint intervals, retention policies, and recovery mechanisms, enabling reliable state management and minimizing data loss in event-driven applications.

blocks.name: monitoring_configuration
blocks.description: (Optional) Describes configuration parameters for CloudWatch logging for an application.

arguments.name: configuration_type

Set this attribute to `CUSTOM` in order for any specified `auto_scaling_enabled`, `parallelism`, or `parallelism_per_kpu` attribute values to be effective.
arguments.llm_summary: The `configuration_type` argument in the `monitoring_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource specifies whether the application uses the default parallelism settings (`DEFAULT`) or custom-defined parallelism settings (`CUSTOM`). Setting this argument to `CUSTOM` enables users to configure advanced scaling and performance parameters, such as `auto_scaling_enabled`, `parallelism`, and `parallelism_per_kpu`, allowing for tailored resource optimization and application behavior.

arguments.name: log_level
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes the verbosity of the CloudWatch Logs for an application. Valid values: `DEBUG`, `ERROR`, `INFO`, `WARN`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `log_level` argument in the `monitoring_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to define the verbosity of CloudWatch Logs for the application, enabling control over the granularity of log data for monitoring and debugging purposes. By specifying values such as `DEBUG`, `ERROR`, `INFO`, or `WARN`, users can tailor log output to align with their operational needs, such as troubleshooting issues or tracking application performance.

arguments.name: metrics_level
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes the granularity of the CloudWatch Logs for an application. Valid values: `APPLICATION`, `OPERATOR`, `PARALLELISM`, `TASK`. The parallelism_configuration object supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `metrics_level` argument in the `monitoring_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to define the granularity of CloudWatch metrics collected for the application, specifying whether metrics are aggregated at the `APPLICATION`, `OPERATOR`, `PARALLELISM`, or `TASK` level. By configuring this argument, users can tailor the depth of monitoring data to align with their performance analysis and troubleshooting needs, enabling more precise insights into application behavior and resource utilization.

blocks.llm_summary: The `monitoring_configuration` block within the `flink_application_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource enables the setup of CloudWatch logging for a Flink-based application, facilitating centralized monitoring and observability. It encapsulates settings to define and manage log streams, allowing users to track application performance, debug issues, and ensure operational insights through detailed log data.

arguments.llm_summary: The `auto_scaling_enabled` argument in the `parallelism_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to control whether the Kinesis Data Analytics service can automatically scale the application's parallelism in response to increased data throughput. Enabling this feature optimizes resource utilization and ensures the application adapts dynamically to fluctuating workloads, supporting common goals like performance scaling and cost efficiency.

arguments.name: configuration_type
arguments.description: (Required) Describes whether the application uses the default parallelism for the Kinesis Data Analytics service. Valid values: `CUSTOM`, `DEFAULT`. Set this attribute to `CUSTOM` in order for any specified `auto_scaling_enabled`, `parallelism`, or `parallelism_per_kpu` attribute values to be effective.
arguments.llm_summary: The `configuration_type` argument specifies whether the application uses the default parallelism settings provided by the Kinesis Data Analytics service (`DEFAULT`) or custom parallelism settings (`CUSTOM`). Setting this to `CUSTOM` enables users to define advanced parallelism-related attributes, such as `auto_scaling_enabled`, `parallelism`, and `parallelism_per_kpu`, allowing for tailored scaling and performance optimization to meet specific workload requirements.

arguments.name: parallelism
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes the initial number of parallel tasks that a Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics application can perform.
arguments.llm_summary: The `parallelism` argument in the `parallelism_configuration` block of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to define the initial number of parallel tasks that a Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics application can execute. Configuring this parameter impacts the application's ability to process data streams concurrently, enabling users to optimize performance and scalability based on workload demands.

arguments.name: parallelism_per_kpu
arguments.description: (Optional) Describes the number of parallel tasks that a Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics application can perform per Kinesis Processing Unit (KPU) used by the application. The run_configuration object supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: "Configures the number of parallel processing tasks a Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics application can execute per Kinesis Processing Unit (KPU), enabling users to optimize application performance and resource utilization by scaling task concurrency within the application's parallelism configuration."

blocks.llm_summary: The `parallelism_configuration` block within the `flink_application_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource defines parameters for optimizing task execution by enabling parallel processing in Apache Flink applications. It encapsulates settings related to task concurrency, such as the degree of parallelism, allowing users to fine-tune application performance and scalability for high-throughput data processing workloads.

"Defines the settings for a Flink-based application within the `application_configuration` of an `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application`, enabling users to configure runtime properties, parallelism, checkpointing, and other operational parameters essential for stream processing and stateful data analytics. This block provides granular control over Flink-specific features, optimizing application performance and reliability in real-time data processing workflows."

blocks.name: run_configuration

blocks.name: application_restore_configuration

arguments.name: application_restore_type
arguments.description: (Required) Specifies how the application should be restored. Valid values: `RESTORE_FROM_CUSTOM_SNAPSHOT`, `RESTORE_FROM_LATEST_SNAPSHOT`, `SKIP_RESTORE_FROM_SNAPSHOT`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `application_restore_type` argument in the `application_restore_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to specify the restoration behavior of the application during startup. It defines whether the application should be restored from a custom snapshot, the latest snapshot, or skip restoration entirely, enabling control over recovery strategies and ensuring alignment with operational or disaster recovery requirements.

arguments.name: snapshot_name
arguments.description: (Optional) The identifier of an existing snapshot of application state to use to restart an application. The application uses this value if `RESTORE_FROM_CUSTOM_SNAPSHOT` is specified for `application_restore_type`. The flink_run_configuration object supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `snapshot_name` argument in the `application_restore_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to specify the identifier of a pre-existing snapshot of the application's state to restore from when restarting the application. This enables the application to resume processing from a defined point in time, supporting use cases like disaster recovery, stateful application continuity, or custom initialization workflows.

blocks.llm_summary: The `application_restore_configuration` block within the `run_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource defines the restore behavior for restarting a Kinesis Data Analytics application. It encapsulates settings that control how the application resumes from a previous state, enabling users to manage state persistence and recovery for fault tolerance or operational continuity during restarts.

blocks.name: flink_run_configuration

arguments.name: allow_non_restored_state
arguments.description: (Optional) When restoring from a snapshot, specifies whether the runtime is allowed to skip a state that cannot be mapped to the new program. Default is `false`. The sql_application_configuration object supports the following:
arguments.llm_summary: The `allow_non_restored_state` argument in the `flink_run_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource controls whether the Flink runtime can proceed with application execution when restoring from a snapshot that contains unmapped or incompatible state. Setting this to `true` enables fault-tolerant recovery by allowing the application to skip unresolvable state, which is useful for scenarios where backward compatibility with previous snapshots is not critical.

blocks.llm_summary: The `flink_run_configuration` block within the `run_configuration` of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource defines the starting parameters for a Flink-based Kinesis Data Analytics application, enabling users to manage how the application initializes and restores its state. This block encapsulates settings related to application restore behavior, such as specifying whether the application should start from a previously saved state or a fresh configuration, providing control over state management and recovery for stream processing workflows.

"Defines the starting parameters for a Flink-based application within the `application_configuration` of `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application`, enabling control over runtime behavior and initialization settings. This block allows users to configure how the application starts, ensuring proper execution and alignment with desired operational requirements."

arguments.llm_summary: The `update` argument within the `timeouts` block of the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource allows users to specify the maximum duration (as a string) Terraform will wait for an application update operation to complete. Configuring this timeout ensures better control over deployment workflows, preventing prolonged or stalled updates during application modifications.

blocks.llm_summary: The `timeouts` configuration block in the `aws_kinesisanalyticsv2_application` resource defines customizable time limits for operations such as creating, updating, or deleting a Kinesis Analytics V2 application. By configuring this block, users can manage operation durations to prevent timeouts in long-running processes, ensuring smoother lifecycle management and better control over application deployment and updates.

attributes.name: create_timestamp
attributes.description: The current timestamp when the application was created.

attributes.name: last_update_timestamp
attributes.description: The current timestamp when the application was last updated.

attributes.name: version_id
attributes.description: The current application version. Kinesis Data Analytics updates the `version_id` each time the application is updated.
